NUEVO LAREDO, Tamaulipas — Construction is officially underway on 62 new homes for families in vulnerable situations in the El Progreso neighborhood, the Nuevo Laredo municipal government announced Thursday, marking the second phase of its Hogar Propio housing program.

According to La Voz NLD, citing municipal and IMVISU data, this stage carries an announced investment of 46.5 million pesos and is being built through the Instituto Municipal de Vivienda y Suelo Urbano (IMVISU). The homes will offer roughly 59 square meters of construction on lots of at least 7 by 18 meters.

The program unfolds in three stages: the first delivered 15 homes, the second is the current 62-home buildout, and a third will add 38 more homes on scattered lots in El Progreso. When all three stages are complete, the project is projected to reach 115 homes, with a total announced investment topping 110 million pesos including construction and urbanization.

During Thursday’s groundbreaking event, led by Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal, officials also handed over a completed home to Ramiro González Hernández, a person with a motor disability — a 58-square-meter home with two bedrooms, living and dining areas, kitchen, full bathroom, carport, laundry area and backyard, built on a 126-square-meter lot.

The municipality is supplying land and resources for the development, with IMVISU operating the program. For families locked out of the private housing market, a deed in hand is about more than square meters: it’s stability. The next steps, according to the city, are finishing construction and delivering the remaining homes so more families can claim their own place to call home.

Sources: La Voz NLD reporting based on Nuevo Laredo municipal government and IMVISU data (Oct. 22, 2026).

title: Nuevo Laredo breaks ground on 62 affordable homes for vulnerable families
